title: THE GREAT OXYGEN DELIVERY
text: A big race is about to begin. But deep inside Maya's body, a tiny delivery team is already on the move! Meet Pip, a curious little explorer, and Ruby, a red blood cell with a very important job.

title: A VERY IMPORTANT MISSION
text: Hello, explorers! Ruby says. Maya's muscles will need more oxygen as she runs. Pip checks Ruby's empty delivery spots. We'd better fill up! Their first stop is the lungs. Come along!

title: SMALL WORLD. BIG ADVENTURE.
text: Real blood cells don't have eyes, voices, or little explorers riding beside them. Oxygen is too small to see like these sparkles. Our cartoon makes an invisible journey easier to imagine.

title: TAKE A BREATH
text: Maya breathes in. Air enters through her nose or mouth, travels down her windpipe, and follows branching airways into her lungs. Pip watches the branches divide. It's an upside-down tree of tunnels!

title: THE TINY AIR-SAC GARDEN
text: The smallest branches end in tiny air sacs called alveoli. Around them are very small blood vessels. Air and blood come close together here, but thin walls keep them separated.

title: OXYGEN CROSSES OVER
text: Oxygen moves across those thin walls into the blood. It doesn't need a door or a robot. This happens naturally. Pip follows our glowing oxygen dots from the air sac toward Ruby.

title: RUBY LOADS UP
text: Inside red blood cells, a protein called hemoglobin can hold oxygen. Think of it as a helper that picks oxygen up and later lets it go. Ruby is ready! Her oxygen cargo will help Maya's muscles keep working.

title: NEXT STOP: THE HEART
tag: Lungs → left side of the heart
text: Whoosh! Blood carries Ruby away from the lungs and back to the left side of the heart. Pip hears a steady beat ahead. Is that a drum? It's a pump, says Ruby. And it's about to give us a push!

title: THE AMAZING HEART PUMP
text: The heart is a strong muscle with four chambers. It squeezes to push blood onward, then relaxes to fill again. One-way valves help control the direction. Our model shows a simplified heart.

title: TWO SIDES. ONE TEAM.
text: The right side of the heart sends blood to the lungs. The left side sends blood to the rest of the body. Ruby has just returned from the lungs, so the left side now pumps her toward Maya's leg muscles.

title: FOLLOW THE BLOOD VESSELS
tag: Arteries carry blood away from the heart
text: Ruby rides through an artery, a vessel carrying blood away from the heart. It branches into smaller vessels. Other red blood cells travel nearby. Nobody needs a steering wheel. The flowing blood carries them!

title: THE NARROWEST STREETS
text: Ruby reaches tiny vessels called capillaries, where blood comes close to body cells. Red blood cells are flexible, helping them fit through narrow spaces. Ruby gently changes shape. Special delivery for the muscles!

title: DELIVERY COMPLETE!
tag: Oxygen moves from blood into tissues
text: Oxygen leaves the blood and moves into muscle tissue. Pip cheers as Ruby's cargo arrives. Remember, oxygen doesn't really glow. We're lighting it up so you can follow its path.

title: HOW CELLS GET ENERGY
tag: Nutrients + oxygen help cells release energy
text: Muscle cells use oxygen to help release usable energy from nutrients in food. Oxygen isn't food or energy by itself. The supplies work together, helping Maya's muscles contract and move her legs.

title: MAYA STARTS RUNNING
text: Maya takes off! Her muscles contract and relax. Her breathing and heartbeat usually speed up to help meet her muscles' needs. Ruby isn't alone. Huge numbers of blood cells keep deliveries moving.

title: THERE'S A RETURN TRIP!
tag: Carbon dioxide travels back in blood
text: Making usable energy also produces carbon dioxide, a waste gas. It enters the blood. Much of it travels in a changed form in blood's liquid part. Time to return to the lungs!

title: BACK THROUGH THE HEART
text: Veins carry blood back to the right side of the heart, which pumps it to the lungs. Ruby has less oxygen, but she's still red! Blood inside your body is never blue.

title: BREATHE OUT. START AGAIN.
tag: Carbon dioxide leaves in exhaled air
text: At the air sacs, carbon dioxide moves from blood into the lungs. Maya breathes it out. Fresh oxygen enters the blood. Ruby loads up again. The loop keeps going, even while you're asleep.

title: YOUR TURN, EXPLORER!
tag: Point to the answer before Pip does
text: Explorer challenge! Which brings air close to blood: lungs or stomach? The lungs! Which pumps blood: heart or bone? The heart! Who helps carry oxygen? Red blood cells, using hemoglobin. Great work!

title: MISSION ACCOMPLISHED
text: Maya finishes, and Ruby starts another trip. Lungs exchange gases. The heart pumps blood. Blood delivers oxygen. What an amazing team! Next time, Pip follows a sandwich to discover what happens after you swallow.
